# b3-v1 card 2 — strategist, 2026-11-21 (saved by Jarvis; the agent cannot write files). Argument only.

Clever Concealment in, Drift of Phantasms out. Non-targeted loss is the larger gap.
1. Targeted protection on Heliod is deep (Auramancy, Blessing, Guardian, Spellskite, Truce); what's missing is a non-GC answer to wrath / edict (003 was that loss; rule 2 "recast at the tax" assumes the board survives). Constant protection is useless against wraths; the cover is a held instant (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance). Concealment phases out Heliod, both Crawlers and the fort in one cast; convoke suits a counter-mana turn.
2. Limit: does not save lands → not an Armageddon answer (pair with the Tithe let-it-resolve line); strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math (snippet only).
3. Kill reach already seven-plus pieces; Alhammarret's Archive a fifth MV-5 artifact buying a third doubler, and doubling only matters while Psychosis Crawler survives → protecting the Crawler outranks reach.
4. Drift: a 3-mana 0/3 defender whose transmute is {1}{U}{U} sorcery speed — effectively a six-mana two-turn tutor for MV 3; Approach/Dig finders already present; least efficient tutor, first slot to give (strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors).
5. Stroke of Genius is self-draw for Psychosis Crawler, not mill; Words of Wisdom the better every-player fit but marginal — hold for card three.
6. Unwind / Rewind: no, counters already deep.
Runner-up: Words of Wisdom for Stroke of Genius.
Dissent: protection density already high → NO CHANGE defensible; Concealment 4 mana or taps scarce creatures; doesn't stop Armageddon; Drift is a 0/3 flying blocker; transmute fetches only MV 3.
Needs: forge-cast-check Concealment; scenario Concealment vs wrath with Crawler + Insight on board.
Caveats: did not read analyst/rules/recon notes; Insight text from card-one note.

# Dawn's Truce gift timing; Clever Concealment and Heliod — rules-question, 2026-11-21 (saved by Jarvis)

(a) Gift draw happens on resolution (702.174j/e), after Truce's cost locked (601.2f) — so it does not cut Truce's own cost but counts for Heliod's discount on later spells this turn. It triggers Smothering Tithe and Scrawling Crawler (121.1). Gifting an opponent with an empty library: they lose at the next SBA check (121.4, 704.5b), after Truce finishes resolving (704.3; inference).
(b) Phased-out Heliod: treated as nonexistent (702.26b) — no discount, no flash grant until he phases in at your untap (702.26a). Concealment's cost is locked before resolution; Heliod's reduction applies at 601.2f, convoke after (702.51b); reduction is generic only, so with three opponent draws {2}{W}{W} → {W}{W}, payable by tapping two white creatures (702.51a).
(c) Hexproof does nothing vs Supreme Verdict / Austere Command (no targets, 702.11b). Indestructible from the gift stops their destroy modes (702.12b), only for permanents present when the gift resolved (611.2c). Winds of Abandon exile is NOT stopped by indestructible; its single-target mode is stopped by hexproof; overload is untargeted. Edicts are NOT stopped by indestructible (701.21a).
